trials.condition: Alzheimer Disease, Senile Dementia, Dementia, Dementia, Alzheimer Type

why: 3 papers report increased neurogenesis (best evidence: rodent, species mouse); 2 papers report decreased neurogenesis; 2 stage(s) have conflicting findings, so the score is reduced. Hypothesis for lab testing, not a treatment claim.

claims.evidence_quote: It has been reported that trichostatin A (TSA) or valproic acid (VPA) can induce the neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic neural stem cells and rat cerebellar granule cells.
claims.title: The histone deacetylase inhibitor trichostatin A induces neurite outgrowth in PC12 cells via the epigenetically regulated expression of the nur77 gene.

claims.evidence_quote: These results show that VPA has the ability to enhance the capacity of NSCs to differentiate into neural precursors and may activate astrocytes, resulting in reactive astrocytes with stem cell qualities.
claims.title: Valproic Acid Stimulates Hippocampal Neurogenesis via Activating the Wnt/β-Catenin Signaling Pathway in the APP/PS1/Nestin-GFP Triple Transgenic Mouse Model of Alzheimer’s Disease - PMC

claims.evidence_quote: VPA Promotes the Proliferation of Neural Stem Cells in the Hippocampus of 3xTgAD Mice To examine the effect of VPA on progenitor cell proliferation, we used BrdU labeling.

claims.evidence_quote: Here, we evaluated the effect of VPA to activate neurogenesis and demonstrated that VPA can induce the proliferation and generation of new neurons in the adult hippocampus in AD.

claims.evidence_quote: In conclusion, this study demonstrated that VPA has a far-reaching effect on the regulation of hippocampal neurogenesis in adult AD mice, leading to an increase in the generation of neural progenitor cells and promoting the differentiation and maturation of neurons.

claims.evidence_quote: VPA enhances neurogenesis and neural stem cell survival—particularly in the hippocampus—while improving synaptic function.
claims.title: Beyond epilepsy: The expanding role of valproic acid in Alzheimer disease therapy – a review - PMC

notes.bbb_note: The label states that valproate's antiepileptic activity is related to increased brain concentrations of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), indicating the drug crosses the blood-brain barrier and acts on the central nervous system.
notes.safety_note: The boxed warning states that life-threatening hepatotoxicity (including fatal hepatic failure, especially in children under two), teratogenicity (birth defects, neural tube defects, neurodevelopmental disorders), and hyperammonemia with or without encephalopathy can occur with valproic acid use.

disclaimer: Hypothesis for lab testing, not a treatment claim.
